correctness.rationale: The unique degree-four wedge vertex separates in round one. Along each of the two otherwise degree-two cycle threads, the round-r color of position i is determined by the unordered pair of distances i and L-i clipped at r; this exact induction determines the last internal split at floor(L/2). If p≠q, endpoint-nearest vertices on the shorter and longer threads remain indistinguishable through round min(p,q)-1 and split at min(p,q); after the shorter length has become visible, pair equality cannot survive between lengths with distinct endpoint-distance sums. Automorphism orbits are reflections within a cycle plus interchange of equal-length petals, exactly the terminal colors. Independently reimplemented the WL partition algorithm with separate encoding and checked all 400 ordered length pairs 3..22, including p=q, small triangles and widely separated lengths. Finite check corroborates, not substitutes for the all-parameter induction.
residual_risks: Uniform initial colors and simple two-cycle wedge required.
Pair-induction supplies infinite conclusion, not the bounded census.

value.rationale: A closed nonconstant exact iteration-depth formula for a canonical bicyclic family, including the sharp cross-length bottleneck and complete orbit recovery, supplies a natural structural benchmark for 1-WL on unicyclic/wedge graphs. Unlike a one-instance census or a trivial degree check, it isolates when branch symmetry persists many rounds as p and q grow. The integer parameter formula can be used to test exact stabilization runtimes; existing general worst-case bounds do not supply these equality cases.
residual_risks: The simultaneous broader rose formula may make the two-petal statement mathematically redundant when the two are published together; this is an attribution/packaging issue, not false mathematics.

final_claim: For integers p,q≥3, two cycles C_p,C_q meeting at one vertex have WL stabilization depth floor(p/2) if p=q, otherwise max(floor(p/2),floor(q/2),min(p,q)); stable colors equal automorphism orbits.
limitations: Only ordinary 1-WL from uniform colors; not general cactus graphs or distinguishing graph pairs.
